key_insight: KaiNinja extends a native single-object 3D generator to produce part-level assets by replacing the single O-Voxel volume with a dual-volume representation that can model touching part interfaces.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, mask-free generation of editable, riggable, and simulation-ready part decomposition without adding a separate segmentation stage.
method: Builds on TRELLIS.2’s native 3D generation backbone instead of post-hoc mesh segmentation.
Introduces a dual-volume O-Voxel form so adjacent parts can be represented at shared interfaces.
Trains on diverse part data, including CAD models and LLM-agent-authored assets, to generate part-level outputs directly.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 40% lower whole-object Chamfer distance and a 16% higher strict part F-score versus other part generation pipelines.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the dual-volume training data, and the representation/training complexity may be higher than a standard single-volume pipeline.
paper_title: Kaininja: Extending Native 3D Generators to the Part Level
